Localisation: You dictate that this culture is to be accepted and fully integrated into your realm. Its people will be your people and will require significant representation. Equal rights come with equal responsibility, and so it is your responsibility to maintain the ever-growing satisfaction of your people.

You dictate that this culture is to be partially integrated into your realm. Its people will have some rights and may even be able to own an establishment, but they are still considered to be second-class citizens at best. With minimal power in politics, the influence of this culture is unlikely to fully materialise within your faction.

You dictate that this lesser culture is undesirable for your realm and its influence must be excised at all costs, even its technologies are considered forbidden. There will be no integration or coexistence. This culture's people and factions will despise you, but why bother considering the sentiment of the inferiors?

You dictate that this lesser culture is to be integrated into your realm with major restrictions. Its community must provide taxation and labour, sometimes with coercion of force. Its people are still not considered citizens and may even be considered property. Nonetheless, this restricted integration will still increase the influence of their culture.

You dictate that this lesser culture is to be tolerated but not integrated into your realm. Its people can live in your territory but possess no civic duty or civil rights. Their community will bring no direct benefit to your faction, but can provide technologies and combatants at a higher cost.
Gold is the resource for constructing buildings and armies. Factions can obtain gold from some buildings' income and alliance trade.
Happiness represents the entire realm's approval of the current situation. It affect faction's gold and supply income. Low happiness can cause your people to rebel!
Supply is the resource for calling units into battle. An army can carry a limited amount and replenish them in owned regions from the reserve or by destroying enemies.

Turn indicates how much time has passed since the beginning of the campaign. Income are added to reserve every turn. Each turn is made up of smaller units called phases that govern the amount of time required to perform actions.

You can view the heroes in your court and their roles. The number of heroes you can have is equal to the number of regions you control. You can dismiss unused heroes to give other heroes an opportunity to join your faction. Heroes who are army commanders cannot be dismissed until you reassign them first.

You can view the current relationship with other factions or offer and accept an alliance. You can also gift gold or supplies to improve your relationship with a faction. The gift effectiveness depends on the amount you give compare to their current reserve and income. Factions with good relationships are more likely to want to be allies and give gifts in return during dire times.

Offer an alliance pact to this faction; an alliance is established when both offer the pact. Allies will help each other in battle and provide gold to their counterpart via trade. The trade income you receive is derived from your ally's supply income.
Note: Reserve army with no commander will not be deployable.
This will delete the army reserve from the list and reassign heroes to courtier status.
This will duplicate the army reserve. Heroes in the army will not be duplicated.
You can set a policy that dictates how you want to deal with culture in your realm.

Restricted cultures integrate less into your society and yield lower influence. Buildings from low integration culture will be less effective, and units will cost more. Accepted cultures demand a proper level of influence and integration.
